checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: 700k view events/sec, and you need the top 100 videos this hour.

options.label: Exact counts per video
options.sub: increment a counter for every video
options.verdict: Perfectly accurate and it does not fit. You are tracking billions of videos to answer a question about a hundred of them, and the counter table becomes the bottleneck for a result nobody needs to be exact.

options.label: Space-Saving with a bounded slot set
options.verdict: Top-K only needs the head of the distribution. A fixed ~10k-slot structure keeps plausible heavy hitters and evicts the rest, giving bounded memory and an error bound instead of an exact count of things that will never rank.

defend.prompt: What did the sketch cost you?

options.label: Counts are approximate, with a bounded error
A video just outside the slot set can be missed
You cannot answer 'exact views for video X' from it
It stops working above a certain event rate

defend.explain: Throughput is exactly what it is good at. You gave up exactness and tail visibility — which is why the sketch answers leaderboards while a separate durable counter answers 'how many views does my video have'.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder

rungs.note: A fixed set of tumbling windows, which is what makes pre-aggregation possible.

rungs.q: Slots kept for candidate heavy hitters
rungs.note: Bounded memory is the whole point — the structure must not grow with the catalogue.

checkpoints.explain: Fixed windows plus a fixed slot budget turn an unbounded counting problem into a constant-memory one.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build the path from a view event to a served leaderboard.
checkpoints.explain: Kafka absorbs the firehose, the aggregator maintains the sketch per window, and the materialised top-K lands in a Redis sorted set that the API reads in O(log n). The batch reconciler corrects drift offline — it must never sit between the event and the leaderboard.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: The 1-hour leaderboard is correct. The all-time leaderboard has stopped moving.
checkpoints.explain: Short windows tumble and free their state; the all-time window never does. Its sketch grows until the aggregator is at 94% heap and can no longer update that window, while the hourly window — which resets — keeps working. All-time needs a bounded structure with periodic compaction, not an ever-growing accumulator.

wrong.Kafka: Lag is normal, and it would delay every window equally rather than just one.
wrong.Redis Sorted Set: Redis is serving whatever it was last given, quickly.
wrong.Event Gateway: Events are arriving fine — the hourly board proves it.
